_about: Relief paint (D-030). Rows in the SITE_SPEC style {v, u, src, tier, note}. The PIGMENTS are those identified at Persepolis (research/RELIEFS_AND_COLOUR.md §3a: B, search extracts of Lerner 2024, Stein 2016, the npj 2026 pigment-lump paper, the Persepolis West residues and the Met squeezes); which pigment goes on which zone is RELIEFS_AND_COLOUR §3b (hair/beard dark blue B/C, royal robe purple with blue hem B, everything else C). The COLOUR VALUES are tier C: CIELAB (D65) of each pure pigment as a matte film on a light ground, reasoned from the ranges published in the conservation literature (recollection; no reflectance or Munsell value was reachable, RELIEFS_AND_COLOUR §4 'OPEN'). They are converted to linear-light albedo in code (CIE 1976 L*a*b* -> XYZ D65 -> linear sRGB), never hand-picked display colours. The PAINT FILM rows model thickness, hiding, gloss and wear (C: no measurement of the Persepolis paint layers was read).

egyptian_blue.note: Egyptian blue (cuprorivaite) at the medium grind used for a full blue: a light, slightly greenish mid blue (coarse grains darker, fine grind paler/greyer); identification at Persepolis B (Lerner 2024, Stein 2016, npj 2026)

dark_blue.note: the 'dark blue' of hair and beard (RELIEFS_AND_COLOUR §3b, B/C): coarse Egyptian blue or lazurite (both identified, B) laid thick; darker and a little more violet than egyptian_blue; black is the alternative reading (§3b)

malachite.note: natural copper carbonate green (malachite) at a medium grind: a light bluish green, never a saturated emerald; identification B (Harvard fragment, plaster, lumps)

cinnabar.note: cinnabar (HgS), the bright red; identification B (Lerner 2024; Stein 2016)

red_ochre.note: iron-oxide red (hematite / red ochre): a brownish red of lower chroma than cinnabar; identification B (Harvard fragment; the red floors)

yellow_ochre.note: iron-oxide yellow (goethite / yellow ochre); identification B (Terrace residues; pigment lumps)

purple.note: the royal robe's 'red or purple' (Iranica 'Clothing ii' citing Tilia, B): no purple pigment is among the identified ones, so a dull violet as mixed from iron-oxide red and a blue (C)

white.note: calcite-dolomite white; identification B (Harvard fragment; lumps)

black.note: carbon black / magnetite; identification B (Harvard fragment; Met squeezes); a matte black film reflects ~3 %, it is not zero

gilt.note: the tone of gilding (D-151): 'gold' among the traces on the reliefs (Iranica 'Persepolis', B) and 'color and gilding' (Nagel 2010, search extract, B); the gilded zones (crowns, jewellery, sceptres, weapon fittings, vessels, the winged ring) C. The relief material draws gilded masses as gold metal (paint.gold); this Lab row is the tone where the leaf is seen as a colour (node previews, far LODs); orpiment (identified, B) would give a similar yellow

film.u: roughness / optical thickness at full film (opacity 1 - exp(-hiding * t)) / thinnest film (fraction) / 1/m / 1/m / fraction of albedo / m
film.note: a matte mineral paint in an aqueous binder (no binder identified; glue or gum assumed): rough (dull, no sheen), opacity 0.97 at full thickness, 0.94 at the thinnest (D-226: an even film; at thickness_min 0.45 and hiding 2.3 the opacity ran 0.64-0.90 at brush scale and dark pigments over the light stone read as camouflage mottling, rubric s7 pass 2); film thickness varies at brush scale (about 2 cm) between thickness_min and 1; pigment grain modulates the albedo by a few per cent; the film stands 0.15 mm proud of the stone (visible only at the edge of a loss). Paint thickness itself was not measured (C)

loss.u: 1/m / noise level above which the film is lost / edge softness / extra loss where the vertex wear is high
loss.note: rare small flaked losses (about 7 mm), on the most worn arrises: a palace in use about 50 years after carving, kept clean and repainted as needed (C); this is not the weathering of the ruin. D-226: level 0.72 -> 0.9, wear_bias 0.45 -> 0.12 (the losses thresholded on the coverage interpolated over a coarse LOD's triangles cut stone-coloured diamonds out of every robe from 4 m: the rubric's mottling)

wear.u: figure units (1 = figure height) / relief-depth units / relief-depth units / fraction
wear.note: paint thins on the raised arrises (D-226: max 0.7 -> 0.25, a kept palace: the film stays edge-bounded to the outline instead of leaving a bare rim round every figure): per carved vertex, convexity = height - mean height within `radius`; paint coverage = 1 - max * smoothstep(conv0, conv1, convexity) (stone shows along outline edges and curl tops). The mean is taken on the LOD's own grid (at least one cell) and the wear is scaled by min(1, radius / cell): a worn outline vertex of a coarse LOD tints triangles a whole cell wide, so without the scale distant figures would look paler than near ones

gold.u: linear RGB reflectance at normal incidence / roughness / 1/m / fraction of F0
gold.note: gilding as gold leaf laid over the carving and burnished (D-151): metal (metalness 1) with the normal-incidence reflectance of gold (the standard physically-based value, linear RGB) and a rubbed, not mirror, surface; a faint grain of the leaf's joins. That the reliefs carried gilding is B (Iranica 'Persepolis': traces of gold; Nagel 2010 'color and gilding'); the technique (leaf on a mordant, foil, or metal attached through drill holes) and the gilded zones are C (Q-231). D-030 drew gold as a yellow matte film because a metal read black in shade without an environment; the material now reflects the skylight into the metal's specular lobe

robe_pattern.note: D-214 (gap audit item 29): garment patterns on the reliefs. The only pattern read for Persepolis is the king's robe (RELIEF-R §3b, B: painted since D-151); the Persian guards' court robes are patterned after the glazed-brick guards of Susa (SUSA-GLAZE, recollection: robes strewn with small rosettes or squares in a lattice, with plain borders: C), the same household troops of the same kings. Paint only: a staggered lattice of small ringed dots (pitch, dot, ring) in white on the robe's colour and a yellow-ochre border (hem_w) along the hem, on the long Persian robe of the figures of `kinds`; the nobles', servants' and delegates' garments stay plain (no pattern read for them: restraint). Motif, size and colours C (Q-427)
